title: First-time home buyer guide for Niagara
excerpt: A step-by-step look at buying your first home in St. Catharines and the Niagara region, from budgeting to closing day.
content:
Buying your first home is a big step, and in Niagara it's one that's still within reach for many buyers priced out of the GTA. Here's a practical roadmap.

1. Know your numbers

Before you look at a single listing, get a mortgage pre-approval. It tells you what you can borrow, locks in a rate for a period of time and shows sellers you're serious. Budget beyond the down payment too: closing costs such as land transfer tax, legal fees, title insurance and moving usually add a few percent of the purchase price.

2. Look into first-time buyer programs

Federal and provincial programs, including land transfer tax rebates and registered savings accounts for home buyers, can make a meaningful difference. Program rules change, so check the current details with your lender, lawyer or accountant.

3. Choose the right community

Niagara is a region of very different towns. St. Catharines offers the widest selection and GO train access, Welland and Port Colborne are known for value, and Thorold has plenty of newer construction.

4. Make a smart offer

Your offer is more than a price: deposit, conditions and closing date all matter. We'll review comparable sales together so you don't overpay, and protect you with the right conditions such as financing and home inspection.

5. Close with confidence

Once your offer is firm, your lawyer, lender and I coordinate the details. On closing day, you get the keys.
